observation.visible_scene: A vertical dark gray board holds a circular wire loop in its center, fixed at the bottom by a small wooden clamp with two screws. A soap film spans the loop: the left part displays iridescent pink/cyan/white interference bands, while the right part is a dark, glossy film that mirrors a blurry figure. A thin metal rod enters from the left edge and its tip rests against the left rim of the loop. The board's edges stay fixed, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The curved boundary between the iridescent left region and the dark right region drifts and oscillates frame to frame, alternately bulging toward the right and toward the left, so the relative sizes of the two regions change.
The iridescent color bands within the left region shift and reconfigure.
The metal rod's vertical position and slight angle change over time (it bobs up and down by a few pixels) while its tip remains near the left rim.
The blurry reflection visible in the dark right film moves and changes shape.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rod's small motion is an intentional adjustment or a vibration, and whether it is the cause of the film-boundary movement.
The film's state before t=0 and after t=2.67 s.
uncertain_details: Whether the dark right region is a very thin 'black' film or simply the bare board seen through an absent film.
Whether the rod tip is in true contact with the rim or merely adjacent to it.
Small apparent shifts could partly be image noise, but the fixed background board argues against camera motion.
